scope: Learned stopping-time consistency on a finite partially observed competing-risk environment. Mechanism pilot, not geometric navigation or Falcon benchmark.
hypothesis: Prefix consistency improves learned conditional event kernels and closed-loop decisions beyond a memory-aware step model and an event model with more training.
inputs: Two visible continuous cues, actual controller age and controller one-hot. Latent intent and future events inaccessible to learned models. No further observations except survival. These inputs are sufficient observed history for this environment.
actions: Choose one fixed controller initially, then continue it or permanently detour. No restart or controller switch. Detour guarantees arrival with additional cost17. Passage adds1; collision adds60.
loss: Observed prefix NLL plus scet-only squared difference between survivor-conditioned event distributions at adjacent prefixes, gradients through both sides. True labels anchor consistency. Event censoring is only at fixed original horizon.
compute: Local NumPy CPU; 24 fits total. event_long gets 3x updates to compare against roughly 3 model passes per SCET update. Actual wall times reported, not asserted equal.

evaluation.access: Once after freezing code/protocol; no tuning on this cohort
evaluation.method: Exact expected closed-loop cost and collision probability under known simulator kernels, no Monte Carlo trajectories. Learned policies use learned kernels only; evaluator uses true kernels. Average seeds within context, paired context bootstrap.

gate: At512 training contexts SCET reduces expected cost by>=5% versus EACH step,event,event_long; paired bootstrap upper cost difference<0 for all three with Bonferroni two-sided99% intervals; collision increase <=0.005 versus each. This is a within-family pilot gate, not SOTA.
integrity: Hash source/config before fitting; save training observations, weights, per-context evaluation and all failed gates. Never modify frozen prior work or resume paused616 benchmark. If no-go, retain outcome and diagnose rather than tuning on evaluation cohort.
